text:
the day that I was taken out of the Special Forces camp which was Body Jab 42, that was our call sign for special forces. My call sign for search and rescue was Tay Nihn. A helicopter call me (Not special forces but me) and said "There are hundreds of enemy digging fighting positions outside our perimeter" I had to run around the french fort and told Sargent Lowry what was going on and I couldn't hear the helicopter and about a half an hour went by and he came running back out to me and said "You son of a bitch! You killed 450 civilians down there" (Wherever down there was, I never saw any of this). No idea why he said this. He then ran off. I immediately thought something was not kosher (not right). I called on my radio the only people I could call was our Headquarters at Ton Son Nuht and asked for anyone in the area, we only had 1 helicopter, asked for Rosethorn 007 to come and get me. That was my command if something was wrong and I had no idea what to do. And they came fast in maybe hour. There was no one there from Special Forces that day except Lowry.

My initial orders were to stay on for search and rescue.
researchNotes: The first full telling of the "450 civilians" day — now a timeline event (data/timeline/1965-08-450-civilians-accusation.json) with a research plan at research/events/450-civilians-nui-ba-den.md. New call signs recorded: Body Jab 42 (the Special Forces camp), Tay Ninh (Larry's search-and-rescue call sign), and Rosethorn 007 (the command helicopter he summoned), with headquarters at "Ton Son Nuht" — his consistent rendering of Tân Sơn Nhứt. The French fort matches the documented colonial ruins on the mountain. The family's long-standing "42" question is now closed: when this comment was written (2026-08-13), Larry confirmed verbally to his son that Body Jab 42 is why he uses that number — the camp call sign was the 42.
